newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil futures falls below $200 a tonne level.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil futures falls below $200 a tonne level.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures fell back through the psycholgical $200 a tonne barrier on Monday in a technical correction after unexpected early strength, brokers said.
February gas oil was traded $2.50 lower at $197.50 a tonne at 1140 GMT, while March Brent was down 17 cents a barrel at $22.09.

"People were surprised at its (gas oil's) strength early on. There was a little bit of buying interest early in the session which kept it up above $200 when most people had expected it to open down," one broker said.
Some attributed the early pick-up in gas oil to uncertainty in the market. Dealers remained bearish for the short term prospects of both Brent and gas oil.

"If it (gas oil) can't manage to recover back up over $200 very quickly then I think it's going to come under further downward pressure. At $1.50 down it's going to attract more nervous selling than support," another broker said.

Some dealers saw Brent in a similar situation, pegging $22 as an important support, and saying a slip below this level would lead to a comparable slide. Brent crude oil broke through a key support level at $22.30 on Friday.
It ended the day 16 cents down at $22.26 a barrel.
